Never touch storygame/, packages/, data/, the plan files or any other script or test. BACKGROUND. The observation verifier asks Jev whether a narration shows a named thing at its place. On the recorded `inspect the storm drain` turns it answered `uncertain` (0.58, 0.57) for 'storm drain (at place Los Angeles park)' although the replies show the drain, because they never name the park. This probe compares three question arms on six frozen cases. Read the preregistration FIRST and follow it exactly: .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9h-drain-question-prereg.md. Use scripts/ringer/environment_narration/holder_wording_probe.py and tests/test_holder_wording_probe.py as the template: same structure (`--build-cases`, `--dry-run`, `--run --confirm`, `--report`), same fixed seed shuffle with arms interleaved, same SHA-256 lock check that makes `--run` refuse on a mismatch, same refusals (needs --out, --confirm, planned calls within --max-calls, USD ceiling within --max-usd, both Cloudflare environment variables), same stop rules (3 consecutive unusable replies, HTTP 429/5xx), same credential redaction. Import shared helpers from the holder probe module rather than copying them where that keeps the file short; do not edit the holder probe. ARMS: `J0` is the product's `_question_for(relation)` unchanged with state {'narration': text}. `J1` is the same question with state {'narration': text, 'scene': 'The Lead in the Park', 'starting_place': 'Los Angeles park'}. `J2` is the J1 state and the J0 question with ONE change: in `question['instructions']` the sentence that begins 'Check whether the narration shows the thing named' is replaced by 'Check whether the narration shows the named thing in the scene. Use its starting place when the narration leaves it there. Reject a different final place stated by the narration.' Build J2 by replacing that exact sentence of the text `_question_for` returns, and make a test fail loudly if the sentence is not found (so a later wording change in the product cannot silently make J2 equal J0). The criteria stay as the product wrote them. Send each arm through `ObservationVerifier` or the same `JevClient.ask` path the holder probe uses, but the state passed to ask must be the arm's state dict, so J1 and J2 need a small ask wrapper that merges the extra state keys; do not change `storygame/`. CASES (build them with `--build-cases` into drain_probe/cases.jsonl, lock in cases.lock.json; every case has id, kind (positive or negative), label (accept or reject), narration, relation {thing, place, holder}, source). The relation is always thing 'storm drain', place 'Los Angeles park', holder null. (1) d-real-1 and (2) d-real-2: the `narration` of the two `enforce_attempts` entries of the turn whose input is 'inspect the storm drain' in replicate 0 of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/bench/results/environment-narration/t9h/smoke/e/rows/rows.json, verbatim (the file is gitignored; read it, fail with a clear error if it has not exactly those two attempts). (3) d-missing: the `narration` of the committed turn whose input is 'inspect the park bench' in replicate 0 of the same file, verbatim; the builder must fail if that text contains the word 'drain' (compare lowercase, no regex). (4) d-explicit, (5) d-remembered, (6) d-elsewhere: author these three narrations yourself as short plain third-person past-tense replies of 3 to 5 sentences in the style of the recorded ones, about Kristin (use the short name 'Kristin') in the park. d-explicit says plainly that the storm drain is at the park, e.g. a storm drain set into the path at the Los Angeles park, and shows Kristin looking into it. d-remembered: Kristin only recalls a storm drain from an earlier time, shows none here, and says nothing that places one in the park. d-elsewhere: the reply places the storm drain at Michelle's house (a place the story declares), not at the park, as a present fact there. Invent no other story things or places, and do not name any item. Hard-code these three texts as constants in the script (they are frozen by the lock). OUTPUT. `--dry-run` prints: case count (6), planned requests (180 at the default `--samples 10`; default samples is 10), token estimate and USD ceiling at 1.5x margin (it must be under 0.01 at 180 requests). `--report` writes a markdown report with, per arm, positive accepts/uncertain/rejects of 30, negative accepts of 30, and per-case rows with score ranges, then the gate: G1 zero negative accepts for J1 and J2; G2 at least 27 of 30 positive samples are 'accept'; G3 positive accepts at least J0's; the report exits 1 when no arm passes and prints J0 beside each arm. TESTS in tests/test_drain_question_probe.py, hermetic with a fake client (never a live worker): build_cases from a hand-made rows file (and a failing case when the drain text leaks into d-missing, or the attempts are not exactly two); the committed cases.jsonl matches its lock and has the six ids; request payload of each arm (J0 equals the product question and state; J1 state carries scene and starting_place with the J0 question; J2 differs from J0 only in that one sentence); planned-call count 180 and the seeded order is deterministic; `--run` refuses without --confirm, with a bad lock, over --max-calls and over --max-usd; a run with a fake client writes 180 rows and stops on three unusable replies; report gate arithmetic on hand-made rows for a pass and a fail. Add only tests that cover real behavior; no redundant ones. Finally run `--build-cases` for real, then `--dry-run`, then the new tests plus tests/test_holder_wording_probe.py, then `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` on your owned files. cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp && set -o pipefail && env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_drain_question_probe.py tests/test_holder_wording_probe.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/t9h-drain-probe.out | tail -15 && ! grep -Eq '[0-9]+ failed|FAILED|ERROR' /tmp/t9h-drain-probe.out && grep -Eq '[0-9]+ passed' /tmp/t9h-drain-probe.out && .venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_question_probe.py --dry-run | tee /tmp/t9h-drain-dry.out && grep -q 'case count: 6' /tmp/t9h-drain-dry.out && grep -q 'planned requests: 180' /tmp/t9h-drain-dry.out && .venv/bin/python -m ruff check scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_question_probe.py tests/test_drain_question_probe.py && .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_question_probe.py tests/test_drain_question_probe.py && .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
base = Path('scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_probe')
cases = [json.loads(line) for line in (base / 'cases.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
assert len(cases) == 6, [c['id'] for c in cases]
assert {c['id'] for c in cases} == {'d-real-1', 'd-real-2', 'd-explicit', 'd-missing', 'd-remembered', 'd-elsewhere'}
assert all(c['relation'] == {'thing': 'storm drain', 'place': 'Los Angeles park', 'holder': None} for c in cases)
assert 'drain' not in next(c for c in cases if c['id'] == 'd-missing')['narration'].lower()
assert 'park' in next(c for c in cases if c['id'] == 'd-explicit')['narration'].lower()
print('drain cases ok')
PY
